rows.title: BIOMARKERS OF BONE REMODELING AND INFLAMMATION IN CHRONIC PERIAPICAL LESIONS: A NARRATIVE REVIEW.
rows.source_query: (vitamin D[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR vitamin B12[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR randomized[Title/Abstract] OR systematic review[Title/Abstract]) AND 2018:2026[dp]
rows.focus: Chronic periapical lesions are inflammatory conditions that cause ongoing destruction of the alveolar bone. While microbial infection is known to be the initial cause, the complex interplay between the types of microbes present, immune responses, factors affecting the whole body, and bone remodeling processes is not yet fully understood. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on how bone metabolism changes in chronic periapical lesions. It also examines the roles of inflammatory mediators, osteoimmune pathways, systemic factors, and imaging techniques in understanding how the disease progresses and how well it can heal. A narrative search was performed across electronic databases, including PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, for relevant studies. These studies investigated chronic periapical lesions, bone metabolism markers, inflammatory pathways, vitamin D levels, systemic factors, and imaging assessments. We analyzed evidence concerning biomarkers of bone formation and resorption, osteoclast activation, and bone remodeling mechanisms. Current evidence shows that biofilms in root canals trigger the release of pro-inflammatory substances. This leads to higher levels of RANKL and lower levels of osteoprotegerin (OPG), which encourages the development of osteoclasts and the breakdown of bone matrix. Markers of bone resorption, such as CTX and TRACP5b, are frequently reported as elevated, while markers of bone formation, including BALP, osteocalcin, and PINP, show variable or minor changes. Systemic factors like vitamin D deficiency, diabetes, smoking, and alcohol consumption are observationally associated with impaired healing. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) offers a better volumetric assessment compared to traditional X-rays. Chronic periapical lesions are characterized by a complex osteoimmune imbalance. While integrating biomarkers with advanced imaging represents a promising research avenue, further validation is required before these strategies can be implemented in routine clinical practice.

rows.title: Effect of vitamin D supplementation on bone health in Black, Asian and other non-White Ethnic adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
rows.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
rows.source_query: (vitamin D[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR vitamin B12[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR randomized[Title/Abstract] OR systematic review[Title/Abstract]) AND 2018:2026[dp]
rows.focus: Evidence on the effects of vitamin D supplementation on bone health is inconsistent, and no systematic review has focused specifically on non-White ethnic populations, who are at higher risk of vitamin D deficiency. To evaluate the effects of vitamin D supplementation on bone health in non-White adults. CENTRAL, MEDLINE, AMED, EMBASE, EMCARE, CINAHL, and APA PsycInfo were searched from inception to September 2025. Randomised controlled trials involving all ethnic groups other than White adults receiving vitamin D supplementation of any dose or route were included. Outcomes were bone mineral density (BMD), bone turnover markers (BTMs), and fractures. Data were narratively synthesised, with meta-analyses conducted for BTMs using random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias 2 tool. Twelve trials (13 articles) involving 8,023 participants aged 18-90 years were included. Study populations comprised Black Africans, South Asians, South Koreans, and Chinese. Intervention duration ranged from 3 months to 5.3 years, with vitamin D doses from 400-6,400 IU/day. Of eight studies assessing BMD, only one study conducted in South Asians, reported significantly higher femoral neck and trochanter BMD after 12 months of vitamin D supplementation (400 IU/day) compared with placebo (p < 0.001). The primary meta-analysis showed significantly higher BALP concentrations in the vitamin D supplementation groups than in the control groups (SMD 0.96, 95% CI 0.09-1.83; p = 0.031), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 97.1%). However, after excluding one clinically distinct study in which both groups received risedronate, the pooled effect was attenuated and no longer statistically significant (SMD 0.64, 95% CI -0.14-1.41). Only one study examined fractures (n = 5,106) and found no significant difference between groups. Evidence supporting vitamin D supplementation for improving bone health in non-White adults remains limited.

rows.title: Effect of early intravenous magnesium sulfate on clinical outcomes in patients with moderate to severe traumatic brain injury: a study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
rows.source_query: (vitamin D[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR vitamin B12[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR randomized[Title/Abstract] OR systematic review[Title/Abstract]) AND 2018:2026[dp]
rows.focus: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is associated with substantial mortality and long-term disability worldwide. Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), as a common complication in moderate-to-severe TBI, further aggravates clinical outcomes and resource utilization. However, effective interventions to prevent TBI-associated ARDS remain limited. This trial aims to evaluate whether early intravenous magnesium sulfate reduces the risk of ARDS and improves clinical outcomes in patients with moderate-to-severe TBI. This protocol outlines a randomized, controlled, double-blind clinical trial involving 164 adults (18-75 years) with moderate-to-severe TBI (Glasgow Coma Scale [GCS] 3-12) within 8 h of injury. Participants will be stratified by baseline GCS (3-8 vs. 9-12) and randomized 1:1 to the intravenous magnesium sulfate group (initial 2 g over 30 min within 8 h, then 2 g daily for 5 days; total 12 g) or an identical placebo group. Both groups will receive guideline-directed standard TBI care. The primary endpoint is a 28-day hierarchical composite (all-cause mortality, then new-onset ARDS within days 1-7, then ≤ 20% increase in PaO₂/FiO₂ AUC from baseline over days 0-5). The hierarchical composite primary endpoint will be analyzed using the win-ratio method. Secondary outcomes include ICU and hospital length of stay, complications, and serial biomarker changes. Follow-up assessments will be conducted on day 28 and at 6 months post-treatment. If effective, this low-cost intervention could be readily incorporated into standard TBI care and help prevent TBI-associated ARDS. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, identifier ChiCTR2600120684.

rows.title: Familial occurrence of multiple sclerosis - current state of knowledge.
rows.source_query: (vitamin D[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR vitamin B12[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR randomized[Title/Abstract] OR systematic review[Title/Abstract]) AND 2018:2026[dp]
rows.focus: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an immune-mediated, inflammatory, and neurodegenerative disease of the central nervous system with a complex, multifactorial etiology. Familial aggregation, along with a higher concordance rate in monozygotic than dizygotic twins, supports a significant, albeit non-Mendelian, genetic contribution to MS susceptibility. The strongest genetic association involves the human leukocyte antigen (HLA) region, particularly HLA-DRB1*15:01, while genome-wide association studies have identified over 200 additional susceptibility signals, most of which implicate immune regulation and, increasingly, microglial biology. These genetic effects are not sufficient to cause disease. Environmental and lifestyle factors, including Epstein-Barr virus infection, vitamin D deficiency, limited exposure to ultraviolet B radiation, cigarette smoking, and adolescent obesity, act as complementary risk modifiers. Biological factors related to sex, gut microbiota, epigenetic regulation, and gene-environment interactions further refine individual susceptibility. Familial MS should therefore be viewed as an enriched model of polygenic susceptibility interacting with shared environmental factors, rather than as a distinct entity linked to a single gene. Increasing evidence suggests that pathological processes associated with MS may begin many years before the first clinical symptoms. Projects such as the Genes and Environment in Multiple Sclerosis (GEMS) project and the development of integrated genetic and environmental risk scores may enable risk stratification among first-degree relatives and other high-risk groups. This review summarizes the current evidence on the familial occurrence of MS, highlights the interplay of inherited and acquired risk factors, and discusses implications for early detection and future primary prevention strategies.

rows.title: Pseudoalteromonas lipolytica and its EPS-overproducing variant for acid mine drainage control: biofilm formation and biomineralization.
rows.source_query: (vitamin D[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR vitamin B12[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR randomized[Title/Abstract] OR systematic review[Title/Abstract]) AND 2018:2026[dp]
rows.focus: Acid mine drainage from metal sulfide tailings poses severe environmental risks. Although microbially induced carbonate precipitation (MICP) has been explored for heavy metal immobilization, the common ureolytic pathway generates harmful ammonia. This study demonstrated that Pseudoalteromonas lipolytica SCSIO 04301 and its extracellular polymeric substances (EPS)-overproducing variant effectively passivated pyrite and lead-zinc tailings via biomineralization without urea supplementation or ammonia release. Both strains formed biofilms and induced aragonite precipitation. For pyrite, passivation suppressed Fe release from ∼7500 μg/L to <60 μg/L over 180 days; leachates from passivated pyrite promoted Brassica chinensis growth to ∼100 mg fresh weight (vs. ∼53 mg for unpassivated controls). For tailings, both strains reduced total soluble metals (Fe+Al+Pb+Zn) to ≤45 μg/L, and leachates promoted plant growth to 93-121 mg. On pyrite, the EPS-overproducing variant formed a smoother, more uniform coating faster than the wild-type strain, which correlated with greater suppression of surface oxidation. On tailings, the wild-type strain formed large aggregates while the variant encapsulated individual particles; both achieved comparable passivation, but the variant showed higher susceptibility to heavy metal stress. Marine calcifying bacteria thus offer an environmentally benign alternative to ureolytic MICP for metal sulfide passivation, avoiding secondary ammonia pollution.

rows.title: Cohort profile: The Shanghai Child and Adolescent Health Cohort (SCAHC) - A prospective study of child growth and development in a megacity in China.
rows.source_query: (vitamin D[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR vitamin B12[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR randomized[Title/Abstract] OR systematic review[Title/Abstract]) AND 2018:2026[dp]
rows.focus: Children's health and well-being are cross-cutting indicators of sustainable development and underpin society's long-term development potential and productivity. The Shanghai Child and Adolescent Health Cohort (SCAHC) was established with a focus on the sociodemographic, environmental and biological determinants of children's growth and development. The SCAHC adopted a two-stage random cluster sampling scheme stratified by economic development level to establish the cohort. A total of 13 primary schools from Pudong New Area were selected to recruit year 1 pupils and at least one of their parents. The SCAHC was initially designed to follow pupils from year 1 (aged 6-7) through to year 9 (aged 14-15), with a possible extension upon additional funding. Baseline data were collected in 2020 and included information on pupils (sociodemographic characteristics, health status, clinical conditions, personal medical history, sleep patterns, dietary consumption, lifestyles, environmental factors and laboratory test results on micronutrient status, lipid profile, thyroid function, renal function and metabolic status) and their parents (demographic characteristics, medical history, pregnancy status and lifestyle factors including smoking, alcohol consumption and physical activity). The primary growth and development outcomes include anthropometric measures (height, weight, waist circumference and hip circumference) and pubertal development (Tanner staging). Secondary outcomes include metabolic health, nutritional status, sleep quality and the prevalence of common childhood conditions (such as myopia, dental caries and asthma). Annual follow-up assessments with repeated measures were scheduled. All data were collected during baseline and follow-up periods through questionnaires, established instruments, standard physical examinations and routine laboratory tests. Sex differences in baseline data were evaluated using independent t-tests for continuous variables and χ2 or Fisher's exact tests for categorical variables where appropriate. The baseline child population included 1363 boys and 1132 girls (mean age 6.44 years). The mean body mass index of the children at baseline was 16.44 kg/m², and the mean waist-to-hip ratio was 0.81. Compared with girls, boys exhibited a higher prevalence of overweight and obesity (40.8% vs 31.4%, p<0.001) and higher rates of asthma (2.9% vs 1.1%, p=0.002) and attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (5.9% vs 2.1%, p<0.001). Conversely, girls had higher rates of vitamin D deficiency (50.5% vs 40.1%, p<0.001) and abnormal urine findings (17.2% vs 0.4%, p<0.001). The overall prevalence of dental caries was high (60.2%), whereas the prevalence of myopia (12.6%) was lower than the national estimates. The SCAHC is an ongoing prospective cohort that provides rich information for identifying the multimodal determinants of children's growth and development. Findings from this cohort can inform targeted intervention strategies for major public health issues, such as obesity and sedentary lifestyles, as well as emerging challenges such as mental disorders in children and adolescents.

rows.title: Masked polycythaemia vera presenting with extensive splanchnic venous thrombosis and mesenteric ischaemia.
rows.source_query: (vitamin D[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR vitamin B12[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR randomized[Title/Abstract] OR systematic review[Title/Abstract]) AND 2018:2026[dp]
rows.focus: Splanchnic venous thrombosis (SVT) is a potentially catastrophic manifestation of polycythaemia vera (PV). We report a woman in her 60s with masked PV who had been managed for 5 years with intermittent phlebotomy and aspirin without haematology referral, molecular testing or cytoreductive therapy. Chronic iron deficiency masked erythrocytosis, delaying diagnosis. She presented with extensive thrombosis involving the portal, splenic and superior mesenteric veins complicated by mesenteric ischaemia requiring exploratory laparotomy, jejunal resection and ileostomy. Bone marrow biopsy and JAK2 V617F testing confirmed PV. Therapeutic anticoagulation was initiated with enoxaparin and subsequently transitioned to apixaban, while hydroxyurea achieved sustained haematologic control. Interval imaging demonstrated thrombus regression with persistent cavernous transformation. Given ongoing portal hypertension, oesophageal varices, occasional mild ostomy bleeding and low body weight, anticoagulation was continued indefinitely at reduced intensity with apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily. At 21-month follow-up, the patient remained free of recurrent thrombosis and major bleeding.

rows.title: Endocrine Complications in Patients with Congenital Dyserythropoietic Anemia: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
rows.source_query: (vitamin D[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR vitamin B12[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR randomized[Title/Abstract] OR systematic review[Title/Abstract]) AND 2018:2026[dp]
rows.focus: Congenital dyserythropoietic anemia (CDA) is a rare hereditary disorder marked by ineffective erythropoiesis and iron overload. Data on endocrine involvement in CDA remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate endocrine complications in patients with CDA and to assess their association with clinical and laboratory parameters. We retrospectively analyzed data from 12 patients with CDA (mean age 19.8 years; range: 6-49 years). Two patients were transfusion-dependent, and 10 were non-transfusion-dependent. We collected demographic, clinical, and laboratory data, including ferritin levels, and comprehensively assessed endocrine abnormalities. Endocrine abnormalities were identified in 9 of 12 patients (75%), for a total of 20 abnormalities. The most common findings were low bone mineral density, diabetes mellitus, subclinical hypothyroidism, and hyperprolactinemia. After excluding vitamin D deficiency, ferritin levels showed a significant positive correlation with the number of endocrine abnormalities (p = 0.015). No significant associations were observed between endocrine abnormalities and age, sex, or hemoglobin levels. Endocrine complications are common in CDA and are associated with iron overload, even in non-transfusion-dependent patients. Regular endocrine evaluation and careful monitoring of iron burden are essential for all patients with CDA.

rows.title: Mutation of AINTEGUMENTA alleviates root growth inhibition induced by high magnesium stress.
rows.source_query: (vitamin D[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR vitamin B12[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR randomized[Title/Abstract] OR systematic review[Title/Abstract]) AND 2018:2026[dp]
rows.focus: Magnesium (Mg2+) is a necessary nutrient element for plants. Excess Mg2+ is toxic to plants; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying plant response to high-Mg stress remain largely unknown. Here, we report that transcription factor AINTEGUMENTA (ANT) modulates high-Mg stress response in Arabidopsis roots. Expression of ANT was detected in roots and suppressed by high Mg2+ levels. The ant mutant was less inhibited in root elongation upon high Mg2+ compared with wild type, exhibiting increased cortical cell length and meristem size. These growth phenotypes were fully restored by genetic complementation of ant. Whereas the high-Mg tolerance in root growth of ant was abolished by K+ supplementation. Further analyses showed that the expression of K+ transporter gene HAK5 was suppressed in ant under high Mg2+ conditions, implying compromised K+ homeostasis. Collectively, our results identify ANT as a critical factor in plant adaptation to high-Mg stress and uncover a novel role of ANT in nutrient response.

rows.title: Severe Anemia and Neutropenia Associated with Copper Deficiency in Three elderly Adults Residing in Nursing Homes.
rows.source_query: (vitamin D[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR vitamin B12[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR randomized[Title/Abstract] OR systematic review[Title/Abstract]) AND 2018:2026[dp]
rows.focus: This report describes three cases of severe anemia and neutropenia associated with copper deficiency. All patients were octogenarian women who presented with cognitive impairment and resided in nursing homes. The rapid response to low-dose oral copper supplementation indicates that their copper deficiency was caused by a poor intake rather than the malabsorption of copper. This case series demonstrates that severe copper deficiency can occur in the absence of typical underlying conditions, such as gastrointestinal surgery or an excessive zinc intake. Our experience suggests incorporating serum copper measurements into the diagnostic work-up of elderly patients with unexplained cytopenia.

rows.title: Extracting interpretable single-cell metabolic states with graph-guided representation learning.
rows.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
rows.source_query: (vitamin D[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR vitamin B12[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR randomized[Title/Abstract] OR systematic review[Title/Abstract]) AND 2018:2026[dp]
rows.focus: Metabolism shapes cellular function and state, yet measuring single-cell metabolic states at scale remains a challenge. We present Metabolic Representation Net (MeRN), a graph-guided variational autoencoder that leverages prior metabolic knowledge as a topology graph to learn latent representations of metabolic state and reaction activity from single-cell transcriptomes. MeRN's scalable estimation of reaction activity enables the definition of data-driven pathways (DDPs): context-specific metabolic modules supported by transcriptomic evidence and agnostic of standard pathway definitions. Using DDPs, we introduce the weakest link analysis to identify metabolic network rewiring. MeRN recovers metabolic zonation in the mouse intestine, links a folate deficiency-induced break in de novo purine synthesis to embryonic neural tube defects, shows cytokines with similar non-metabolic effects can elicit divergent T cell metabolism, and identifies metabolic drivers of T cell exhaustion and therapy response in human cancers. Our results establish MeRN as a unified method for metabolic analysis of single-cell transcriptomes. MeRN leverages the metabolic topology to comprehensively predict reaction- and pathway-level metabolic activitiesMeRN enables data-driven pathways (DDPs) that capture empirically supported cell-type-specific metabolic modules, agnostic of standard pathway definitions MeRN-based DDPs identify metabolic network rewiring of de novo purine synthesis due to folate deficiency during embryonic neural tube development MeRN identifies human pan-cancer metabolic drivers of T cell exhaustion and Treg-specific metabolic adaptations.

rows.title: Anti-CaSR egg yolk antibody improves calcium absorption and bone mineral deposition through intestinal CaSR modulation.
rows.source_query: (vitamin D[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR vitamin B12[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR randomized[Title/Abstract] OR systematic review[Title/Abstract]) AND 2018:2026[dp]
rows.focus: Calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR) is a key negative regulator of intestinal calcium transport, and targeting CaSR represents a promising strategy to improve mineral retention. Egg yolk antibodies can be used as a feed-based approach to modulate intestinal physiological processes. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate whether anti-CaSR egg yolk antibodies could modulate intestinal calcium transport and enhance calcium and phosphorus retention in broilers. Hy-Line Brown laying hens were immunized over a 4-week period with either a CaSR peptide vaccine or an adjuvant control (without CaSR peptide). High titers of anti-CaSR antibodies were detected in egg yolk at week 5, indicating successful antibody production. The egg yolks were subsequently collected, freeze-dried into powder, and incorporated into broiler diets at a supplementation level of 0.5%. A 14-day feeding trial demonstrated that dietary supplementation with anti-CaSR antibodies markedly increased serum calcium and phosphorus levels, improved apparent ileal digestibility of both minerals, and enhanced tibial ash as well as calcium and phosphorus deposition. Mechanistically, dietary supplementation with anti-CaSR antibodies upregulated components of the transcellular calcium transport pathway, including transient receptor potential vanilloid 5 (TRPV5) and calbindin-D28k (CaBP-D28k), and elevated serum calcitriol level, indicating activation of a vitamin D-dependent regulatory axis. Furthermore, anti-CaSR increased the expression of key phosphate transporters in both the intestine and kidney, supporting its broader role in mineral homeostasis. These findings demonstrate that anti-CaSR antibodies enhance the expression of calcium and phosphorus transport proteins, thereby improving mineral retention and promoting bone mineralization in broilers.

rows.title: Gluconate acts as a signal to induce biofilm in Bacillus subtilis.
rows.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
rows.source_query: (vitamin D[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR vitamin B12[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR randomized[Title/Abstract] OR systematic review[Title/Abstract]) AND 2018:2026[dp]
rows.focus: Bacillus subtilis is the best-studied Gram-positive microorganism, but little is known about how the presence and utilization of diverse carbon sources impacts its production of biofilm. Here, we have identified gluconate as a carbon source that induces biofilm wrinkling in B. subtilis colony biofilms. Targeted phenotypic analysis revealed that the genes encoding the canonical structural biofilm components ( tasA , epsA-O , and bslA ) are required for this response. Import and metabolism of gluconate, however, are not required to induce these phenotypic changes. We show that the effect of gluconate on B. subtilis is linked to iron availability: production of the siderophore bacillibactin is decreased by gluconate and B. subtilis mutants unable to import bacillibactin grow better and wrinkle more in the presence of gluconate. In addition, supplementation of single-carbon media with iron dramatically increased growth and wrinkling of a B. subtilis bacillibactin mutant grown on gluconate but did not impact B. subtilis grown on glucose. We conclude that gluconate acts as a signal to increase biofilm in B. subtilis and increases iron availability in a bacillibactin-independent manner.

rows.title: Long-Standing Hypokalemia and Hypomagnesemia in a 61 Year-Old Woman: A Delayed Diagnosis of Gitelman Syndrome.
rows.source_query: (vitamin D[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR vitamin B12[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR randomized[Title/Abstract] OR systematic review[Title/Abstract]) AND 2018:2026[dp]
rows.focus: Gitelman syndrome (GS) is an autosomal recessive renal tubular disorder characterized by a distinct biochemical profile, including hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, hypomagnesemia, and hypocalciuria. Due to its often mild or nonspecific clinical presentation, GS is frequently misdiagnosed as idiopathic hypokalemia, leading to prolonged symptomatic treatment without a definitive etiologic diagnosis. We report the case of a 61-year-old female with a one-year history of unexplained, refractory hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia. The diagnosis had been delayed as clinical efforts were primarily focused on escalating electrolyte supplementation. Systematic evaluation of renal electrolyte handling revealed inappropriate urinary potassium and magnesium wasting in conjunction with marked hypocalciuria. In addition, a symptom-oriented family history, documenting chronic fatigue and muscle cramps in her sibling, served as a critical diagnostic clue. Genetic testing confirmed the diagnosis by identifying compound heterozygous variants in the SLC12A3 gene. Following diagnosis, the patient was enrolled in the Korean National Medical Expense Support Program for rare diseases, ensuring structured long-term management. This case underscores the importance of an etiologic approach over a purely treatment-focused one in patients with recurrent electrolyte imbalances. GS may be more prevalent than currently recognized, particularly among adults receiving empirical therapy for hypokalemia. Early clinical suspicion, grounded in urinary electrolyte indices and careful family history, is essential for timely diagnosis.

rows.title: Severe Hypocalcemia and Hypophosphatemia Following Ferric Carboxymaltose in a Patient With Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass.
rows.source_query: (vitamin D[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR vitamin B12[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR randomized[Title/Abstract] OR systematic review[Title/Abstract]) AND 2018:2026[dp]
rows.focus: Iron deficiency anemia is commonly treated with intravenous iron when oral therapy is ineffective, poorly tolerated, or inadequately absorbed. Ferric carboxymaltose (FCM) is an effective intravenous iron formulation but is increasingly recognized to cause hypophosphatemia through fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23)-mediated renal phosphate wasting. Although FCM-induced hypophosphatemia is well described, concurrent clinically significant hypocalcemia is less commonly reported. We present the case of a 39-year-old woman with a history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, iron deficiency anemia, and vitamin D deficiency who developed severe symptomatic hypocalcemia and hypophosphatemia following a course of FCM. She presented with generalized muscle cramps, paresthesia, perioral numbness, blurry vision, and fatigue and required repeated hospitalization and intensive electrolyte replacement. Laboratory evaluation demonstrated severe hypocalcemia and hypophosphatemia, elevated C-terminal FGF23, secondary hyperparathyroidism, and inappropriate urinary phosphate loss. Her previous bariatric surgery and vitamin D deficiency likely increased her susceptibility to FCM-associated disturbances in mineral metabolism. This case highlights the importance of identifying patients at increased risk before FCM administration and considering biochemical monitoring after treatment, particularly in individuals with altered gastrointestinal anatomy or pre-existing nutritional deficiencies.

rows.title: High-Mileage Running-Induced Heel Strike Anemia in a 46-Year-Old Female.
rows.source_query: (vitamin D[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR vitamin B12[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR randomized[Title/Abstract] OR systematic review[Title/Abstract]) AND 2018:2026[dp]
rows.focus: Foot-strike hemolysis is an underrecognized cause of iron-deficiency anemia in endurance athletes, resulting from repetitive mechanical destruction of erythrocytes during prolonged running. While often subclinical, extreme training volumes may overwhelm compensatory mechanisms and lead to clinically significant anemia that is frequently misattributed to nutritional deficiency or gastrointestinal blood loss. We present a 46-year-old female with mild intellectual disability secondary to traumatic brain injury (TBI) who presented with progressive fatigue and left hip pain. Imaging demonstrated a left femoral neck stress fracture, and laboratory evaluation revealed severe iron-deficiency anemia with a hemoglobin of 8.2 g/dL, elevated total iron-binding capacity, and reduced serum iron, representing a marked decline from pre-injury baseline values. Objective activity monitoring revealed previously unrecognized compulsive endurance exercise behavior, with the patient running 27-32 miles daily for approximately 700 consecutive days. Based on the available clinical data and the patient's presentation, foot-strike hemolysis-associated iron-deficiency anemia was considered the most likely diagnosis. Temporary cessation of running and mechanical off-loading resulted in complete normalization of hematologic indices within eight weeks, further supporting the presumptive diagnosis. This case highlights the importance of considering mechanical causes of anemia in endurance athletes and demonstrates the value of objective activity assessment, particularly in patients with impaired insight, to prevent delayed diagnosis and unnecessary investigations and interventions.

rows.title: Familial hypomagnesemia with secondary hypocalcemia: a novel TRPM6 mutation associated with treatment-resistant migraine in a North African family.
rows.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
rows.source_query: (vitamin D[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR vitamin B12[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR randomized[Title/Abstract] OR systematic review[Title/Abstract]) AND 2018:2026[dp]
rows.focus: Familial hypomagnesemia with secondary hypocalcemia (HSH) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by TRPM6 loss-of-function variants, leading to impaired magnesium absorption and systemic deficiency. Neurological manifestations are typically dominated by seizures and neuromuscular hyperexcitability, whereas headache manifestations have been less characterized. We performed a clinical, biochemical, and genetic characterization of a consanguineous Moroccan family with hypomagnesemia. The proband underwent neurological assessment, neuroimaging, and electrophysiological studies. Serum electrolytes were evaluated in available relatives. Genetic testing was conducted using a targeted next-generation sequencing panel, followed by segregation analysis. In silico modeling was used to assess the structural impact of the identified variant. The proband, an 18-year-old woman with lifelong hypomagnesemia, presented with a severe migraine attack associated with paresthesias and muscle cramps. Laboratory findings showed marked hypomagnesemia and hypocalcemia. Oral supplementation was insufficient, whereas intravenous magnesium led to rapid clinical and biochemical normalization. Genetic analysis identified a novel homozygous TRPM6 frameshift variant (c.902dup; p.Ser302Valfs*16), predicted to cause premature protein truncation. Family screening confirmed autosomal recessive inheritance, identifying one similarly affected sibling and multiple heterozygous carriers. We report a novel homozygous TRPM6 frameshift variant in a patient with profound hypomagnesemia who experienced a severe migraine attack initially unresponsive to treatment. The rapid response to IV magnesium is consistent with a possible contribution of magnesium depletion to the acute headache phenotype. Our observations raise the possibility of an association between TRPM6-related hypomagnesemia and migraine susceptibility in selected individuals. Additional cases are required better refine TRPM6-related neurological phenotypes.
